topic: Assessing the Sick and Deteriorating Child
parentTitle: Assessing the Sick and Deteriorating Child
title: National PEWS, parental concern and Martha's Rule
blurb: Score the national PEWS chart, choose the escalation level from the highest single trigger, act within the set time, and respond to carer concern and Martha's Rule calls.
question: A 2-year-old on a children's ward has a PEWS of 2, but when asked the carer question his father says, 'He's worse than this morning; I think a doctor should see him.' What escalation does the national PEWS chart require?

teach.h: One national system, four age charts
teach.body: The national Paediatric Early Warning System (PEWS) for England was published in November 2023 by NHS England with RCPCH and RCN. It is a track and trigger chart for general children's wards, with four age-band charts: 0-11 months, 1-4 years, 5-12 years, and 13 years and over. It is not a triage tool. Escalation is triggered by the score AND by carer concern, clinical intuition, AVPU change and specific concerns such as sepsis.
teach.cite: NHS England national PEWS observation and escalation charts (2023); RCPCH SPOT FAQ

teach.h: What is scored and what is recorded
head: Scored
Recorded, not scored
teach.caption: High flow, CPAP and BiPAP score the maximum 4 for oxygen delivery. Always score a value even if it is 'normal for this patient' (for example a child with cardiac disease).

teach.h: Escalation levels (identical on all four charts)

bands.label: LOW: inform nurse in charge; reassess within 60 min
MEDIUM: ST3+ medical review within 30 min; reassess within 30 min

head: Level
Other triggers (any one is enough)
rows: New suspicion of sepsis; carer or clinician wants a medical review
AVPU change to V; new suspicion of septic shock; carer or clinician wants a Rapid Review
AVPU P or U; abnormal pupils; carer says the child has collapsed or significantly deteriorated
teach.caption: Respond at the HIGHEST level reached by a change in ANY ONE criterion.

teach.body: At each set of observations, ask the parent or carer: 'How is your child different since I last saw them?' Record Worse, Same, Better, Asleep or Unavailable. Parents know their child best. A carer whose words suggest the child needs a clinical review escalates to Medium, whatever the PEWS score.

steps.label: Reassess
steps.sub: Within the set time; follow the plan

rows.label: Purpose
values: Rapid review for worry about deterioration
Another view on a diagnosis or plan

teach.caption: Three components: ask at least daily how the patient is; staff can call a different team at any time; the same route for families. Required in adult and paediatric inpatient settings by 31 March 2027.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Noah, 2, on the ward
items: Noah, 2, with gastroenteritis, scores PEWS 2 at 14:00. Asked the carer question, his father says, 'He's worse than this morning; I think a doctor should see him.'
Nurse Ella records 'W'. Carer words suggesting the child needs a clinical review trigger Medium, whatever the score.
She informs the nurse in charge, requests an ST3+ medical review within 30 minutes using ISBAR, starts continuous SpO2 and plans to reassess within 30 minutes.
She tells Noah's father what will happen and, if he is still worried and feels unheard, how to use Martha's Rule.

teach.text: Do not average or add triggers: respond to the HIGHEST level from any single criterion. A PEWS of 3 with a child now responding only to pain is an EMERGENCY (2222), not Low.

items: Four charts: 0-11 months, 1-4 years, 5-12 years, 13+. Temperature, AVPU and pain are recorded but not scored.
Low 1-4: reassess within 60 min. Medium 5-8: medical review and reassess within 30 min.
High 9-12: Rapid Review within 15 min. Emergency 13+: 2222 'Paediatric Medical Emergency'.
Carer question and clinical intuition trigger escalation regardless of the score.
Martha's Rule: families and staff can call a different team for a rapid review; not a second opinion.

summary: You can now score the national PEWS chart, choose the escalation level from the highest single trigger, deliver the required response within the set time, and treat carer concern and clinical intuition as formal triggers alongside Martha's Rule.

A.q: Harvey, 6, scores a PEWS of 6 on the national chart. There are no other triggers. What response does the chart require?
options: Inform the nurse in charge; reassess within 60 minutes
Request ST3+ review; reassess within 30 minutes
Call for a Rapid Review within 15 minutes
Make an immediate 2222 emergency call
A.why: A score of 5-8 is Medium: review by the nurse in charge, request an ST3+ medical review within 30 minutes, reassess within 30 minutes with continuous SpO2.

whyNot.2: Rapid Review within 15 minutes is the High (9-12) response.

A.q: Mia, 3, has a temperature of 39.2°C, HR 120, RR 28 and SpO2 97% in air. A student asks how temperature contributes to the PEWS score. What is correct?
options: It scores 2 points when above 39°C
It scores 1 point when above 38°C
It adds to the score in infants under 1
It is recorded but does not score
A.why: On the national PEWS chart temperature, AVPU and pain are recorded but not scored. Temperature still informs the sepsis prompt.

whyNot.0: Temperature is not a scored parameter.
whyNot.1: Temperature is not a scored parameter at any level.
whyNot.2: Temperature is not scored on any of the four age charts, including the infant chart.

A.q: Lily, 8 months, has pneumonia with a PEWS of 10. What escalation level is this?
options: Low
Medium
High
Emergency
A.why: A PEWS of 9-12 is the High level: immediate nurse in charge review and a Rapid Review within 15 minutes.

B.q: Ethan, 5, with suspected meningitis, now responds only to pain. His PEWS is 7. What should the nurse do?
options: Call 2222 and state 'Paediatric Medical Emergency'
Request a medical review within 30 minutes
Call for a Rapid Review within 15 minutes
Repeat observations within 30 minutes
B.why: A change in AVPU to P or U is an Emergency trigger whatever the score; the response is the highest level reached by any criterion.

whyNot.1: This is the Medium response based on the score of 7, but AVPU P triggers Emergency.
whyNot.2: Rapid Review is for AVPU change to V or High; P or U is Emergency.
whyNot.3: Reassessment alone is far below the required response.

B.q: Sophie, 4, is on high-flow nasal oxygen for bronchiolitis. A newly qualified nurse is unsure how to score oxygen delivery on the PEWS chart. What is correct?
options: Score by the percentage of oxygen delivered
Score 0, as high flow is not oxygen
Score the maximum of 4 for oxygen delivery
Leave the box blank and document high flow
B.why: The national chart states that high flow, BiPAP and CPAP score the maximum of 4 on oxygen delivery.

whyNot.0: Respiratory support is scored at the maximum, not by percentage.
whyNot.1: High flow scores the maximum, not 0.
whyNot.3: The chart requires a score, not a blank.

B.q: Amir, 7, has congenital heart disease and his usual SpO2 is 82%. Today his SpO2 is 82% and he looks well. How should this be scored on PEWS?
options: Score 0 as this is normal for him
Leave it unscored and write a comment
Use the adult NEWS2 Scale 2 instead
Score it as the chart directs
B.why: The national PEWS chart says always score the relevant value even if it is normal for the patient (for example a cardiac patient); there is no derogation.

whyNot.0: Scoring 0 is a derogation the chart does not allow.
whyNot.2: NEWS2 is for people aged 16 and over, not children.

C.q: Noah, 2, has a PEWS of 2. When the nurse asks the carer question, his father says, 'He's worse than this morning; I think a doctor should see him.' What is the required escalation level?
options: Low, based on the PEWS of 2
Medium, as the carer's words trigger a review
High, as the carer is concerned
Emergency, as the child is described as worse
C.why: Carer words suggesting the child needs a clinical review trigger Medium, whatever the score; respond at the highest level from any single criterion.

whyNot.0: The score alone would be Low, but the carer trigger is higher.
whyNot.2: High is triggered when the carer's words suggest a Rapid Review is needed; this description fits clinical review.
whyNot.3: Emergency is triggered when the carer says the child has collapsed or significantly deteriorated.

C.q: Amira, 9, has been reviewed twice for abdominal pain after an operation. Her father remains very worried she is getting worse and feels no one is listening. What should the nurse do?
options: Explain how to call Martha's Rule for a rapid review
Remind him the team has reviewed her twice today
Suggest he asks for a second opinion at outpatients
Reassure him that her PEWS is low so she is safe
C.why: Martha's Rule lets families who remain worried about deterioration, and feel unheard, request a rapid review from a different team. The nurse should also escalate her own concerns.

whyNot.1: Previous reviews do not remove the family's right to escalate.
whyNot.2: Martha's Rule is not a second opinion; it is an urgent rapid review for deterioration.
whyNot.3: A low PEWS does not override family concern, which is itself a trigger.

C.q: Jacob, 13, is admitted to a general children's ward. His PEWS is 4 at 10:00. The nurse has a strong sense he is 'just not right' and feels he needs a Rapid Review. Which chart and response apply?
options: 5-12 years chart; reassess within 60 minutes
Adult NEWS2 chart; call outreach within 30 minutes
13+ chart; reassess within 60 minutes
13+ chart; Rapid Review within 15 minutes
C.why: At 13 he uses the 13 years and over chart. Clinical intuition that a Rapid Review is needed is a High trigger whatever the score, so a Rapid Review within 15 minutes is required.

whyNot.0: At 13 he belongs on the 13+ chart, and intuition raises the level above Low.
whyNot.1: NEWS2 is used from 16; he should be on the paediatric chart.
whyNot.2: Right chart, but the clinical intuition trigger requires the High response, not Low.

reteach.title: The highest flag wins
reteach.question: If the score says Low but the parent says 'collapsed', which do you follow?

blocks.body: Think of each trigger as its own alarm: the score, AVPU, the carer's answer, your intuition, a new suspicion of sepsis. Whichever alarm is loudest decides the response. A Low score never cancels a louder alarm.

blocks.text: 60 / 30 / 15 / immediate: Low reassess within 60 min, Medium within 30, High Rapid Review within 15, Emergency 2222 now.

explain.body: Four national age-band charts: 0-11 months, 1-4 years, 5-12 years, 13+. Scored: HR, RR, respiratory distress, SpO2, oxygen delivery, systolic BP, CRT. Recorded not scored: temperature, AVPU, pain.

test.q: Which national PEWS chart should be used for a child aged 12 years and 6 months?
options: 1-4 years
13 years and over
5-12 years
Adult NEWS2
test.why: The 5-12 years chart covers children up to their 13th birthday.

whyNot.0: 1-4 years is for toddlers and preschool children.
whyNot.3: NEWS2 is for people aged 16 and over.

explain.body: Low 1-4: inform NIC, reassess within 60 min. Medium 5-8: ST3+ review and reassess within 30 min. High 9-12: Rapid Review within 15 min. Emergency 13+: 2222.

test.q: What PEWS score range is the High escalation level?
options: 13 or more

explain.body: Carer question, clinical intuition, AVPU change and suspicion of sepsis each trigger a level. Respond at the highest level reached by any single criterion.

test.q: A child with a PEWS of 3 becomes responsive only to voice. What level applies?
options: Low
High
Medium
Emergency
test.why: An AVPU change to V is a High trigger, regardless of the score.

whyNot.0: The score alone is Low, but AVPU V triggers High.
whyNot.2: Medium triggers include sepsis suspicion and review requests, not AVPU V.
whyNot.3: Emergency is for AVPU P or U.

explain.body: Patients asked at least daily how they are; staff can call a different team at any time if concerned and not responded to; the same route for patients, families and carers. Not a second opinion. Required in adult and paediatric inpatient settings by 31 March 2027.

options: A rapid review route for families and staff
A right to a second opinion on a diagnosis
A national early warning score for children
A complaint process run by the hospital
test.why: Martha's Rule gives patients, families, carers and staff a route to request a rapid review from a different team when worried about deterioration.

whyNot.1: NHS England states Martha's Rule is not a second opinion.
whyNot.2: PEWS is the early warning system; Martha's Rule is an escalation route.
whyNot.3: It is a safety escalation, not a complaints process.
